title: Radio waves: fields, speed and wavelength
blurb: A radio wave is a pair of fields moving at light speed, and its wavelength is just 300 ÷ frequency.

T3B01.why: A radio wave is an electric field and a magnetic field locked together at **right angles**.

T3B02.why: Polarization is the direction of the **electric** field. Electric field vertical means vertical polarization.
T3B02.trap: The magnetic field is also there, but it is not what defines polarization.

T3B03.why: Every radio wave is built from an **electric field** and a **magnetic field**.
T3B03.trap: Voltage and current live in wires and circuits; fields are what travel through space.

T3B04.why: Radio waves travel at the **speed of light**, the same as any electromagnetic wave.

T3B05.why: Speed is fixed, so faster wiggling means each wave is shorter: **higher frequency, shorter wavelength**.

T3B06.why: Wavelength (m) = **300 ÷ frequency (MHz)**. Example: 150 MHz gives 2 m.
T3B06.trap: Don't multiply, and don't use hertz: the 300 only works with MHz.

T3B07.why: Bands are named by their approximate **wavelength in meters**: 146 MHz is about 2 m, so it's the 2-meter band.

T3B08.trap: 30–300 *kHz* is a different band entirely: check the unit.

T3B09.why: UHF is **300 – 3000 MHz**, one step up from VHF.

T3B10.why: HF is **3 – 30 MHz**, the lowest of the three.

T3B11.why: Light speed is about **300,000,000 meters per second**.
T3B11.trap: The mph choices are the wrong unit and too slow; 150,000,000 m/s is half the real speed.

T3B12.why: In free space **all** radio frequencies travel at the same speed. Frequency changes wavelength, never speed.
